_note:
DRESSED 2026-08-10, then GIVEN ITS SUPERSTRUCTURE AND ITS SHEER 2026-08-10. This is the GENERAL-PURPOSE hull, and every decision below is made for a boat a player fits out for a dozen jobs rather than for one.

1. THE 8x8 m PLATE AT y=3.0 IS NOW THE ROOF OF SOMETHING. It, its stairwell and the stair up to it were already here and are load-bearing for tests/vessel_render_capture.gd's fall-protection walk, so not one of them moved. What was missing is the deckhouse they are the roof and the companionway OF: four raked plates under it, z 8.6->16.2 at the deck and tucked 0.06 m inside the plate's edge all round, so the plate reads as an EAVE rather than as a lid. The front rakes 0.56 m FORWARD over the foredeck, the sides flare 0.28 m, the aft bulkhead is reverse-raked 0.28 m. Never a box out of walls: the room primitive was deleted and this is the raked plate that replaced it.

2. THE WHEELHOUSE IS SMALL AND SET BACK. 5.10 x 4.90 m on an 8 x 8 m deck - 18% of LOA - so a 1.3-1.7 m walkway runs right round it inside the guardrails that were already there, and the companionway arrives inside it. 2.45 m to the eaves; the screen rakes 0.55 m forward, the aft bulkhead reverse-rakes, the roof falls 0.25 m aft. WINDOWS ARE THE SAME PART ON EVERY TIER, 2026-08-10. They were not: the wheelhouse had a dark band and the lower tier had punched holes with nothing behind them, which at every range read as pale rectangles the value of the plating - as holes, not as glass. One rule now: the run is ONE band; a dark GLASS pane sits 0.10 m inboard of the shell plane and laps 0.12 m past the opening all round so the reveal is 0.19 m of real depth and no daylight leaks round the pane; cream MULLIONS stand in the reveal at the shell plane; and the wheelhouse band gets CORNER PILLARS, which is what closes the notch two recessed panes leave where they meet at a corner. A DOOR keeps its punched opening and gets no glass, because a door is a hole you walk through - tests/plan_interior_test.gd marches a player capsule through the aft deckhouse door of this vessel and out again to prove it.

3. THE BULWARK IS A SHEER EDGE, not three walls. walls 1/2/3 were a constant 1.0 m bar from z=6 aft, sitting 0.26 m OUTBOARD of the hull at z=6 because they were axis-aligned and the hull is not. They are one `edges[]` sheer_band now: the PLAN line is the hull's own deck edge, the Y curve is authored, and the run closes round the stem. The curve is DELIBERATELY FLATTER than the trawler's - low point 1.05 m at z=18 (64% aft), 2.32 m at the stem against the trawler's 2.85 - because this is a general workboat, not a heavy-weather boat. wall 4, the last fragment of the deckhouse the room purge took, is deleted: it was a 6 m panel standing alone on the aft deck.

4. THE HULL SIDE HAS RELIEF. A second `edges[]` run is the RUBBING STRAKE - 115 mm proud x 200 mm tall with a light top chamfer. Its plan line is the shell at the STRAKE'S OWN HEIGHT, measured off StructureEdge.deck_half_beam_at rather than taken from the deck, because the topsides flare and a band hung on the deck's half-beam would float up to 120 mm off the plating. It CANNOT follow the sheer - deck_y is flat, which is the whole reason the cap carries the curve - so instead it rises as the shell allows, 0.58 m under the deck aft and 0.30 m at the stem.

5. COLOUR DOES VALUE WORK, FOR FREE. Five steps dark to light - navy plating, grey rubbing strake, dark boat deck, light grey lower tier, near-white wheelhouse - plus ONE saturated accent, and the accent is a colour the boat already wore: the cap rail is the same yellow as the crane and the davits. Squinted, that is five values instead of the two this fixture had.

6. THE RIG STANDS ON SOMETHING AGAIN. The mast, its radome, whips, floodlights and masthead light, the two sidelights and the four-piece exhaust stack all stood in OPEN AIR at y=3.0 after the room purge. The mast is stepped on the wheelhouse roof and everything it carries is solved from its 6-degree aft rake; the sidelights are on the wheelhouse sides; the stack is on the boat deck abaft it. The three stays deleted with the old deckhouse are BACK, because there is a roof to belay them to - a stay made fast to nothing is the one thing a rig may not have.

7. THE AFT DECK IS LEFT CLEAR ON PURPOSE. Two flush hatch tops and the existing bitts, davits and fenders, and nothing else: 11 m of open working deck abaft the house with a knuckle-boom crane forward of it is what makes this hull general-purpose. A winch would have made it a trawler.

COST, on RenderingServer's own counters over the four canonical views: DRAW CALLS UNCHANGED at 8 undressed / 16 with the shadow pass, because a swept bulwark, a rubbing strake, twenty-eight plates and a dozen colours all bucket on MATERIAL alone. TRIANGLES ROSE, and by a lot: a superstructure and two swept runs are geometry, and tests/vessel_render_capture.gd's COST_BUDGET entry for this fixture (12 600) was measured when it had neither. See the report for the measured number.
